extraction_note: This FY2021 10-K is from Fortress Transportation and Infrastructure Investors LLC (pre-spin-off form of FTAI Aviation). Filing covers Aviation Leasing (commercial aircraft engines), Jefferson Terminal (crude/refined products), Ports and Terminals (Repauno/Long Ridge), and Transtar (freight railroads). The filing contains ZERO references to Pentagon Program Elements, DoD program names, military aircraft engines, military aircraft platforms, J-Book line items, or specific defense customers. The cohort metadata note about 'military adjacency via LM2500 marine engines / CFM56 modules' is NOT borne out in this filing — CFM56 references appear nowhere in the sliced text, LM2500 references appear nowhere, and there are no DoD customers named. Pentagon J-Book is therefore the primary verifier ONLY by absence: no J-Book-grounded claims to verify. We extract the closest analogues (forward-looking commercial-aviation pipeline, infrastructure pipeline) and the spin-off thesis, plus control claims, to exercise the framework. Net result expected: this ticker should fall OUT of the J-Book divergence cohort because the company makes no J-Book-grounded claims.

claims.claim_text: FTAI announced in Q4 2021 it intends to spin off its infrastructure business as a separate publicly traded entity in Q2 2022, with the infrastructure entity remitting approximately $800 million in cash to FTAI as part of the separation.
claims.subject: FTAI Corporate Strategy
claims.object_value: Infrastructure segment as separate public co with $800M cash remit
claims.source_quote: In the fourth quarter of 2021, the Company announced that it intends to spin off its infrastructure business as a separate publicly traded entity... The infrastructure entity intends to remit to FTAI approximately $800 million in cash as part of the separation... The spin off transaction is expected to be completed during the second quarter of 2022.

claims.claim_text: FTAI's Aviation Leasing segment generates equipment-leasing revenue from commercial aircraft and aircraft engines held for long-term lease (total equipment-leasing revenue of $335.6M in 2021).
claims.subject: Aviation Leasing segment
claims.object_value: $335.6M equipment leasing revenue in 2021 from commercial aircraft/engines
claims.source_quote: The Aviation Leasing segment consists of aircraft and aircraft engines held for lease and are typically held long-term... Total equipment leasing revenues 335,583

claims.claim_text: FTAI's Transtar segment, acquired in July 2021, comprises five freight railroads and one switching company providing rail service to certain manufacturing and production facilities; Transtar represented 16% of total assets and 13% of revenues in 2021.
claims.subject: Transtar segment
claims.source_quote: In July 2021, we acquired Transtar... Transtar is comprised of five freight railroads and one switching company that provide rail service to certain manufacturing and production facilities... Transtar represented approximately 16% of our total assets and 13% of our total revenues as of and for the year ended December 31, 2021.

claims.claim_text: FTAI's Jefferson Terminal segment is a multi-modal crude and refined products terminal that had a two-year pipeline capacity agreement obligating fixed marketing fees of $10.2M per year, with crude marketing revenues having dropped to $0 in 2021 (vs $166M in 2019) after Jefferson exited the crude marketing strategy in Q4 2019.
claims.subject: Jefferson Terminal segment
claims.object_value: crude marketing strategy; revenues went from $166M (2019) to $0 (2021)
claims.source_quote: Crude marketing revenues decreased $8.2 million. In 2019, Jefferson directly sourced crude from producers in Canada... Jefferson exited this crude marketing strategy in the fourth quarter of 2019 as a result of unfavorable oil spreads

claims.claim_text: FTAI's Ports and Terminals segment includes Repauno, a 1,630-acre deep-water port along the Delaware River with an underground storage cavern, multi-purpose dock, rail-to-ship transloading system; the company is redeveloping it as a multi-purpose, multi-modal deepwater port.
claims.subject: Repauno (Ports and Terminals)
claims.object_value: multi-modal deepwater port (1,630 acres, Delaware River)
claims.source_quote: Repauno, which is a 1,630 acre deep-water port located along the Delaware River with an underground storage cavern, a new multipurpose dock, a rail-to-ship transloading system and multiple industrial development opportunities

claims.claim_text: FTAI's Long Ridge investment is a 1,660-acre multi-modal port along the Ohio River with rail, dock and multiple industrial development opportunities, including a power plant in operation.
claims.subject: Long Ridge (equity-method investment)
claims.object_value: 1,660-acre multi-modal port + power plant in operation
claims.source_quote: an equity method investment (Long Ridge), which is a 1,660 acre multi-modal port located along the Ohio River with rail, dock, and multiple industrial development opportunities, including a power plant in operation.

claims.claim_text: FTAI states a number of aviation lessees have been placed on non-accrual status as of December 31, 2021, with overall portfolio exposure limited by maintenance reserves and security deposits valued at $145.5 million.
claims.subject: Aviation Leasing credit risk
claims.object_value: $145.5M maintenance reserves and security deposits against lessee defaults
claims.source_quote: A number of these lessees have been placed on non-accrual status as of December 31, 2021; however, we believe our overall portfolio exposure is limited by maintenance reserves and security deposits which are secured against lessee defaults. The value of these deposits was $145.5 million as of December 31, 2021.

claims.claim_text: FTAI has $3.3 billion of outstanding principal debt and $1.2 billion of interest payment obligations as of December 31, 2021, with $100.5M principal and $185.4M interest due in next twelve months.
claims.subject: Debt obligations
claims.source_quote: As of December 31, 2021, we had outstanding principal and interest payment obligations of $3.3 billion and $1.2 billion, respectively, of which, $100.5 million and $185.4 million, respectively, are due in the next twelve months.
